note: Estimate derivation graph. Every derived estimate must trace to source estimates. Prevents untraceable numbers. Cycles are invalid.

transformations.description: Filter EU-27 employer enterprises 10+ to manufacturing + regulated sectors 50+ employees. Apply NACE C, J (partial), M (partial) and size class 50+.
transformations.reason: FactBounty target segment: enterprises making high-stakes B2B procurement decisions requiring independent evidence.

unitCompatibilityCheck.notes: Both estimates use unit-b2b-buyer-enterprise (STOCK). Filter does not change unit type.

transformations.description: Multiply enterprise stock by assumed annual events per enterprise to derive annual event flow. UNIT CONVERSION: STOCK (enterprises) → FLOW (events/year). This is the critical conversion.
transformations.reason: FactBounty billing unit is procurement-decision-event (FLOW), not enterprise (STOCK). Stock must be converted to flow via frequency assumption.

unitCompatibilityCheck.notes: INPUT unit: unit-b2b-buyer-enterprise (STOCK). OUTPUT unit: unit-procurement-decision-event (FLOW per_year). Explicit unit conversion performed — not a silent mix. Frequency assumption labelled HIGH sensitivity.

periodCompatibilityCheck.notes: Enterprise stock 2022; events assumed 2024. Small period mismatch; enterprise count relatively stable.

lineages.notes: This lineage records the unit conversion from enterprise-stock to event-flow. The multiplier (2-10) is unobserved and dominates uncertainty. A WITNESS survey asking 'how many qualifying procurement decisions did your organization make last year?' would directly measure this factor.

transformations.description: Multiply active EPC count by dispute prevalence rate to get annual dispute events. PREVALENCE RATE IS UNKNOWN.
transformations.reason: Affected = Eligible × dispute_rate. Rate is the binding unknown.

unitCompatibilityCheck.notes: INPUT: unit-epc-engagement (STOCK). OUTPUT: unit-mv-settlement-event (FLOW per_year, at rate 1 settlement/EPC/year). Explicit unit conversion. Dispute rate is the filter making AFFECTED a flow subset.

lineages.notes: Derivation cannot complete because input factor (dispute rate) is NOT_YET_MEASURED. Output correctly carries NOT_YET_MEASURED state. This is not a failure — it is the honest result.

transformations.description: Multiply annual dispute events by price per engagement to get annual revenue opportunity.
transformations.reason: TAM = events × price. Both inputs are currently unknown/scenario.

unitCompatibilityCheck.notes: INPUT: events_per_year × EUR/event = EUR_per_year. Correct unit arithmetic.

lineages.notes: Revenue TAM cannot be computed because both dispute rate and price are unknown/scenario. This lineage documents WHY the TAM is NOT_YET_MEASURED rather than providing a false number.
